subject: Inference fit lab — prep, slot & scope questions
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@pressa.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: elena@pressa.ai
Date: 2026-03-19T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-discovery: next steps for a hands-on lab

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the discovery session yesterday — Elena and I found the discussion on latency/cost tradeoffs really helpful. We'd like to move to a focused technical lab to validate inference fit and the proposed runbook (KV cache behavior, batching, and fallback routing). Our primary goals are:
- Verify end-to-end latency on our sample traces (avg and p95)
- Exercise prefix/KV caching on our top-4 prompt templates
- Walk through rollback/fallback behavior if a quantized variant falls back

Can your team run a 90-minute hands-on lab the week of Mar 23? Ideal times for us: Tue 3/24 morning (PST) or Wed 3/25 afternoon (PST). Also attaching our short architecture constraints doc.

Attachments: pressa_arch_requirements.pdf (1 page)

Warmly,
Samir
Director of ML Engineering
Pressa.ai
From: dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@pressa.ai>, Elena Gomez <elena@pressa.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-19T10:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: next steps for a hands-on lab

Hi Samir — great to hear. We can definitely run a focused lab to validate the items you listed. Quick notes and asks before we lock a slot: 

1) Scope: we'll plan for a 90-minute session — first 45 minutes hands-on with benchmark traces, second 45 for runbook walkthrough and Q&A.
2) Data & traces: please confirm a single S3 share or a link to a small trace file (<= 500MB). If you prefer, we can run with a synthetic trace to validate latency envelope but real traces are ideal.
3) Environment: will this run against your private VPC (Private deployment) or our hosted sandbox? For initial validation hosted sandbox is faster; if you need VPC we need a little extra prep (VPC peering/firewall rules).
4) Suggested slots (PST): Tue 3/24 09:30–11:00, Tue 3/24 11:30–13:00, Wed 3/25 14:00–15:30. Pick one and we'll send a calendar invite.

I've cc'd Ben (solutions engineering) and Marissa (Customer Success) — Ben will drive the bench and runbook demo. Marissa will coordinate pre-call prep and share the runbook template.

Thanks,
Dylan
Sr. Pre-Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@pressa.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-19T12:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: next steps for a hands-on lab

Samir — quick technical detail from my side:
- For KV/prefix caching validation we need sample prompt templates and the top 10 token-length distribution (or a few representative examples).
- If you expect to test quantized variants, please confirm model family (e.g., MPT-7B, Llama2-13B) so I can stage the correct binary and quantization artifacts.
- If using hosted sandbox, we'll provision a session with a pinned model version to avoid runtime variance.

I can run the bench and capture token-level latency, cpu/gpu utilization, and cache hit-rate. If we run in your VPC, please add ben@redwood.com to the temporary IAM role we discussed in discovery (or share a short-lived presigned object containing the traces).

My availability: Tue 3/24 09:30–12:00 and Wed 3/25 13:30–16:00 (PST). If you take the Tue morning slot we can iterate on the runbook in-session.

—Ben
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Gomez <elena@pressa.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-19T14:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: next steps for a hands-on lab

Thanks — we want the Tue 3/24 11:30–13:00 slot please. Two clarifications:
- We'll share a small sample trace (two prompt families, ~200MB) via an S3 pre-signed URL by Monday noon.
- Pressa will run the test against Redwood hosted sandbox for speed. If results look good, we may request a VPC run later.

Also: Samir will be joined by our infra lead (internal) and I might bring our product manager for the runbook review. Neither will present, just listening in.

—Elena
Senior Engineering Manager, Pressa.ai
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@pressa.ai>, Elena Gomez <elena@pressa.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-19T17:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: next steps for a hands-on lab (confirmed)

All — confirmed for Tue 24 Mar 11:30–13:00 PST. Calendar invite sent: https://calendar.redwood.com/meet/BN-3521-slot-1

Prep checklist (please action by Mon 3/23 12:00 PST):
- Samir/Elena: S3 presigned URL with traces (pressa_arch_requirements.pdf attached to this thread)
- Samir: list of top-4 prompt templates and expected p95 SLA targets
- Ben: stage sandbox with MPT-7B quantized and FP32 variants; capture baseline metrics
- Dylan: short runbook deck and failure/fallback playbook (I'll attach runbook-template-v2.md)

Attachments: runbook-template-v2.md (preview)

If anything changes, flag here and we'll reschedule. Looking forward to it.

Best,
